finalReport.rawFindings:
--- CRITICAL FINDINGS ---

[RT-1] High-frequency client publish => huge fan-out risk
File: src/controller/NetcodeController.tsx (L1-L220)
Evidence: The client calls sendUpdate every 100ms and publishes both position and animation DataPacket_Kind.LOSSY (two publishes per tick), producing ~20 publishes/sec per client; with room sizes (create-room sets maxParticipants: 20) this multiplies to thousands of forwarded messages per second.  
Impact: LiveKit or network egress will be overwhelmed as participants grow (CPU/egress or instance limits hit first), causing message drops, high latency, or service degradation for entire room.  
Fix: Reduce publish rate, merge/delta updates, use interest management (send only to nearby clients), or offload aggregation/authority to the server/LiveKit data channel with rate limits.

[RT-2] LOSSY packets with no sequencing/replay → unrecoverable stale state
File: src/controller/NetcodeController.tsx (L1-L220)
Evidence: Position/animation updates use DataPacket_Kind.LOSSY and there is no sequence numbers, snapshots, ACKs, or join-time reconciliation logic; reconnects or dropped packets are not replayed.  
Impact: Clients that briefly disconnect or lose packets can show persistent stale positions/animations and never catch up, breaking UX and causing inconsistent world state.  
Fix: Add sequence numbers/timestamps, send periodic reliable snapshots (RELIABLE) or implement a join-time state snapshot endpoint so clients can reconcile missed updates.

--- WARNING FINDINGS ---

[RT-3] publishData awaits with no backpressure policy
File: src/controller/NetcodeController.tsx (L1-L220)
Evidence: publishData is awaited and guarded by a simple lock (positionSendLock/animationSendLock) but has no timeout, batching, drop-policy, or slow-client handling.  
Impact: Slow network or blocked publish calls stall the send loop (locks prevent new sends) so updates drop or client update frequency collapses under congestion.  
Fix: Add bounded queues, non-blocking best-effort sends, timeouts, or drop-oldest policy and expose backpressure/health to UI.

[RT-4] Serverless/module-level LiveKit init + mock fallback masks outages
File: src/lib/livekit.ts (L1-L220)
Evidence: LiveKit RoomServiceClient is initialized at module load with retries and a roomServiceFallback that returns mock data when connection fails.  
Impact: In serverless deployments the cached client may not persist across cold starts, and the mock fallback can silently hide LiveKit outages (UI shows empty rooms) instead of failing fast or routing to alerts.  
Fix: Remove or restrict mock fallback in production, surface health check errors, and make RoomService initialization explicit per-request with robust retry/backoff and monitoring.

[RT-5] Webhook DB writes are synchronous per event (join/leave)
File: src/app/api/webhooks/livekit/route.ts (L1-L220)
Evidence: Each participant_joined/participant_left handler does immediate db.room.update/increment on the webhook request path.  
Impact: Spiky room churn generates many DB writes (and transactions), risking DB load and delayed webhook handling which can desynchronize user counts or cause timeouts.  
Fix: Buffer or batch updates (Redis counters or queue) and apply aggregated deltas to the DB, and make webhook handling idempotent/async.

--- INFO ---

[RT-6] Token endpoints issue client tokens directly (no server authority replay)
File: src/pages/api/connection_details.ts and src/pages/api/universe/create-room.ts (L1-L220)
Evidence: API routes mint AccessTokens with canPublishData and, in universe flows, bypass auth checks for guests and return ws_url/token directly.
